clue.text: Term she's said to have organised?

definitions.text: Term she's said to have organised?

parts.words: Term she's said to have organised?
parts.note: the school term is run by the woman in charge of a girls' school, so she is the one who organises it

explanation.surface: A question about who arranged some fixed period or word.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a girls' school is responsible for planning and running each school term.

clue.text: Executing a stroke that's eye catching

definitions.meaning: in cricket or golf, a hook is a stroke sending the ball sharply leftwards
a hook fastens by catching on its eye, as in a hook-and-eye fastener

explanation.surface: Someone playing a shot so striking that everyone looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a shot in cricket and golf, and a hook catches the small metal loop called an eye on clothing.

clue.text: A form of security to protect one grand woman

indicators.note: one thing protecting another wraps around it, so these letters go inside the security word

parts.note: bail is money lodged as security for a released prisoner; the clue's 'A' is taken separately as A
one is the Roman numeral I
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A bond that safeguards one distinguished lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts one grand inside the security word. An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, after a character in a Beaumont and Fletcher play.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a woman's name, and once a general term for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Game bowl splinters

parts.note: a match is a game played between sides
in the game of bowls, each bowl is called a wood

explanation.surface: A competitive game of bowls breaks into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls is a British pastime in which the heavy balls rolled along the green are known as woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood smashed into tiny fragments, as in 'smashed to matchwood'.

clue.text: Crack, mostly a substance that's sniffed

indicators.note: most of the word, not all of it, is kept, so its final letters are dropped

parts.note: solvent abuse means sniffing glue or similar chemicals

explanation.surface: A drug-taking picture: crack and solvents being inhaled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests the drug, but it is the definition in its puzzle-cracking sense. 'mostly' drops the last two letters NT from SOLVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a problem or code is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Go rapidly to seed here in Cheshire

parts.note: to run is to move quickly on foot
corn is the seed of cereal plants

explanation.surface: Plants quickly bolting in a garden in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England; Runcorn is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is an industrial town on the Mersey within Cheshire's borders.

clue.text: Stirs up rising, short of energy and endurance

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to animate is to rouse or stir up
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone agitated, lacking energy and stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ANIMATES into SETAMINA; 'short of' then removes E to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the capacity to keep going for long.

clue.text: One rarely misses, an opening

parts.note: describes a theatregoer who habitually attends the opening performance of every new show

explanation.surface: Someone whose aim is reliable, finding a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatregoer who makes a habit of attending premieres seldom misses an opening night.

clue.text: One using sarcasm — it's unusually hard to take at first

indicators.note: the hard word is taken to the front, coming first before the rearranged letters

parts.note: iron stands for hardness, as in an iron will

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sardonic person finds it hard to accept things at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the clue's IT'S, and 'to take at first' puts the hard word in front of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone using sarcasm says the opposite of what they mean, the essence of irony.

clue.text: Neckline?

parts.note: read literally as a line or cord worn around the neck, rather than the cut of a garment's collar

explanation.surface: A question about the shape of a dress collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord hung round the neck to carry a whistle, knife or pass is literally a line for the neck.

clue.text: Bottle of booze

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage, so this is bravery that comes from drink

explanation.surface: Simply a bottle containing alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means nerve, so the clue means courage got from alcohol, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage summoned by drinking alcohol is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Turn both taps, covering a vegetable

indicators.note: the outer letters cover the article, sitting around it

parts.note: to spin is to turn round
a basin's two taps are marked C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: Turning on both taps to wash a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' makes the turn plus both taps sit around the clue's 'a'; the taps are the hot and cold of a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Self-important type (English) got one's goat finally

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I plus S

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A conceited Englishman was finally irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: To get someone's goat is an idiom for annoying them, the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who thinks and talks mostly about themself is self-important.

clue.text: Cricket side batting — over goes to him

indicators.note: over signals turning the letters round, read in reverse

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
in cricket, the batting side is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket team batting as the over passes to a particular player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sounds like cricket, but reverses LEGIN. The definition is 'him', a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel is a man's first name, so it can stand for an unnamed male person.

clue.text: A bench, possibly, provided by cricket side for scorer

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A cricket team lends a bench to its scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket scorer keeps the score; here a scorer is a composer of music. 'possibly' rearranges A BENCH to ENBACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach composed operettas, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Two classical elements of strong spirit

parts.note: the ancient Greeks counted four elements: earth, air, fire and water
the ancient Greeks counted four elements: earth, air, fire and water

explanation.surface: Two of the ancient elements that make up a bold character.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a jocular term for strong alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: European with his own article in plant

parts.note: a German is a European
der is the masculine definite article in German, the European's own language

explanation.surface: A European grows a plant featuring his own article.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb or shrub of the mint family.

clue.text: Dismissed from teaching — instant uproar

indicators.note: something dismissed from a word is sent away, removed from it

parts.note: instruction is teaching
inst. is short for instant, meaning this month in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone sacked from teaching sparks an immediate row.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or row.

clue.text: Almost offensive to Ambassador and one of his suite

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, with the final letter dropped

parts.note: an offensive is an attack
an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE

explanation.surface: Rude to an ambassador and a member of his staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective, but is the noun meaning attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a diplomat on an ambassador's staff.

clue.text: Capital character invested in business

indicators.note: something invested in a thing is put inside it, as money is put into a business

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a business
an air is a character or manner, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A person of character has put money into a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Article in daily on lower classes is a travesty

indicators.note: the article is placed in among the other letters
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in daily
D and E are the lowest social grades in the British classification
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about the poor is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a newspaper, but means a cleaning lady; 'in' puts the article between her and the lower classes, which follow her ('on').
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a travesty of the real thing.

clue.text: Single mark on publication is a colophon

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: single is one, the Roman numeral I
M is short for mark, the former German currency
print is publication, as in appearing in print

explanation.surface: A single mark on a published book is its colophon.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's imprint is its name or emblem on a book, which is what a colophon shows.

clue.text: Old historian giving Roman emperor about a chapter

indicators.note: about means around, so the emperor's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Titus was emperor of Rome from AD 79 to 81

explanation.surface: An ancient historian writing a chapter on a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian who chronicled the early empire.

clue.text: Nail a youth

definitions.meaning: a small headless nail or brad used by glaziers
a young lad, a slip of a boy

explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small tapering brad, and also dated slang for a young man.

clue.text: Cover with modern American performer

parts.note: a rapper performs rap, a genre born in modern America

explanation.surface: A cover version recorded with a US hip-hop artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a covering for something, such as a sweet.

clue.text: Powerful coach has to complain about run

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly
ca. is short for circa, about
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A strong trainer has to protest about a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a trainer; here it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled rail carriage, a coach with its own power.

clue.text: Damaging material can make one furious

explanation.surface: Ruining fabric can drive someone into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripping cloth damages it, and a violent rage is described as a tearing one.

clue.text: Lower sleeve in man's article of clothing

parts.note: under means lower

indicators.note: the sleeve word goes inside the man word

parts.note: a gent is a man
a sleeve is the arm of a garment

explanation.surface: A lowered sleeve on a man's piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear such as a vest or slip is worn beneath other clothing.
